stories.title: Discovery returns safely after the STS-121 mission
stories.summary: The shuttle landed at Kennedy Space Center after nearly thirteen days in orbit and 5.3 million miles traveled.
stories.alt: Space Shuttle Discovery launches on the STS-121 mission

stories.title: Fighting in Lebanon grows into a major regional crisis
stories.summary: Cross-border attacks and escalating hostilities plunged southern Lebanon and northern Israel into weeks of war.
stories.alt: Smoke rises over Tyre, Lebanon, during an air strike in 2006

stories.title: World leaders meet in St. Petersburg for the G8 summit
stories.summary: Energy, security, North Korea, Iran, and the new crisis in Lebanon crowded the summit agenda.
stories.alt: Leaders pose for the official photograph at the 2006 G8 summit

stories.title: Italy defeats France to win the World Cup
stories.summary: A 1-1 final went to penalties in Berlin, where Italy captured its fourth men's world championship.
stories.alt: Italy and France play in the 2006 FIFA World Cup final

stories.title: Alvin and Jason Jr. return to explore the Titanic
stories.summary: Researchers made the first crewed dives to the wreck and captured close-up images of the ship's bow and interior.
stories.alt: The bow of the Titanic on the North Atlantic seafloor

stories.title: America celebrates the Statue of Liberty centennial
stories.summary: Liberty Weekend marked the statue's restoration and the relighting of its torch in New York Harbor.
stories.alt: President Ronald Reagan speaks during the Statue of Liberty centennial celebration

stories.title: NASA releases its Challenger crew report and transcript
stories.summary: The report followed months of recovery and investigation after the January loss of Challenger and its seven astronauts.
stories.alt: Smoke and debris from Space Shuttle Challenger after launch

stories.title: Chernobyl reshapes the global nuclear-safety debate
stories.summary: The reactor explosion and fire spread radioactive material across a wide area of Europe and transformed nuclear policy.
stories.alt: The damaged Chernobyl nuclear power station after the 1986 disaster

stories.title: Medicare benefits begin for more than 19 million Americans
stories.summary: The new federal health-insurance program began covering nearly the entire population age 65 and older.
stories.alt: President Lyndon Johnson signs the Medicare bill beside Harry Truman

stories.title: Gemini X launches toward a record-setting mission
stories.summary: John Young and Michael Collins docked with an Agena target, reached a new crewed-altitude record, and completed two spacewalks.
stories.alt: An Agena target vehicle fires its engine above Earth during Gemini X

stories.title: A week of unrest exposes deep inequality in Cleveland's Hough neighborhood
stories.summary: Clashes, fires, and four deaths followed years of segregation, poor housing, unemployment, and neglected city services.
stories.alt: The intersection of East 79th Street and Hough Avenue in Cleveland

stories.title: England hosts the World Cup and wins its first title
stories.summary: The hosts defeated West Germany 4-2 after extra time at Wembley, with Geoff Hurst scoring a historic hat trick.
stories.alt: England and West Germany enter the pitch for the 1966 World Cup final

stories.title: The United States recognizes Philippine independence
stories.summary: American sovereignty ended and the independent Republic of the Philippines entered formal diplomatic relations with the United States.
stories.alt: The Philippine flag is raised during the July 4, 1946 independence ceremony

stories.title: Operation Crossroads tests atomic weapons at Bikini Atoll
stories.summary: Two detonations studied nuclear effects on a fleet of target ships while displacing Bikini's residents from their homeland.
stories.alt: The Baker underwater nuclear test sends a huge column of water above Bikini Atoll
stories.credit: U.S. Department of Defense / public domain

stories.title: Bombing destroys a wing of Jerusalem's King David Hotel
stories.summary: The Irgun attack struck offices of the British administration and killed British, Arab, and Jewish victims.
stories.alt: A damaged wing of the King David Hotel after the 1946 bombing

stories.title: The Nuremberg tribunal weighs evidence against Nazi leaders
stories.summary: The international trial established a vast documentary record of aggressive war, war crimes, and crimes against humanity.
stories.alt: Stacks of captured German records prepared as evidence for the Nuremberg trials

stories.title: Carter G. Woodson establishes Negro History Week
stories.summary: Woodson's educational campaign challenged schools to teach Black history and eventually grew into Black History Month.
stories.alt: Historian Carter G. Woodson in an academic portrait

stories.title: Robert Goddard launches the first liquid-fueled rocket
stories.summary: The two-and-a-half-second flight climbed only 41 feet, but it demonstrated the technology that would power the Space Age.
stories.alt: Robert Goddard stands beside an early liquid-fueled rocket

stories.title: Route 66 joins Chicago and Los Angeles in a new highway system
stories.summary: The 2,400-mile route connected rural communities, cities, and the growing culture of American automobile travel.
stories.alt: Historic U.S. Route 66 highway shield

stories.title: Gertrude Ederle becomes the first woman to swim the English Channel
stories.summary: The nineteen-year-old American finished in 14 hours 31 minutes, breaking the existing men's record by nearly two hours.
stories.alt: Gertrude Ederle during her 1926 English Channel swim
stories.credit: Le Miroir des sports / public domain
